sentences.zh: 凡八百九十二部，一萬二千二十八卷。

translations.literal: In all, eight hundred ninety-two titles, twelve thousand twenty-eight scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: 892 titles in all, 12,028 scrolls.

translations.literal: 【Conclusion】The books of the Three Dynasties, having passed through Qin's burning, were nearly all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: 【Conclusion】The books of the Three Dynasties were nearly all destroyed in Qin's burning.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝、河間王始重儒術，于灰燼之餘，拓纂亡散，篇卷僅而復存。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han and the King of Hejian first gave weight to Confucian learning; from the ashes they gathered what was lost and scattered, and but a few chapters and scrolls survived anew.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han and the King of Hejian first revived Confucian learning; from the ashes they gathered what had been lost and scattered, and only a few chapters and scrolls survived.

sentences.zh: 劉更生石渠典校之書，卷軸無幾。

translations.literal: The books that Liu Gengsheng collated at the Stone Canal Pavilion amounted to only a few scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The books Liu Gengsheng collated at the Stone Canal Pavilion amounted to only a few scrolls.

sentences.zh: 逮歆之《七略》，在《漢藝文志》者，裁三萬三千九百卷。

translations.literal: By the time of Xin's Seven Summaries, as recorded in the Han Bibliographic Treatise, there were only thirty-three thousand nine hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Liu Xin's Seven Summaries, as recorded in the Han Bibliographic Treatise, there were only 33,900 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 後漢蘭台、石室、東觀、南宮諸儒撰集，部帙漸增。

translations.literal: In Later Han, the scholar-officials of the Orchid Pavilion, Stone Chamber, Eastern View, and Southern Palace compiled and collected, and the number of titles and bundles gradually increased.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han, scholar-officials at the Orchid Pavilion, Stone Chamber, Eastern View, and Southern Palace compiled and collected, and the number of titles and bundles gradually increased.

sentences.zh: 董卓遷都，載舟西上，因罹寇盜，沉之於河，存者數船而已。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhuo moved the capital, the books were loaded onto boats and sent west; they fell prey to bandits and robbers and were sunk in the river — only a few boatloads survived.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhuo moved the capital, the books were loaded onto boats and sent west; bandits struck, and they were sunk in the river — only a few boatloads survived.

sentences.zh: 及魏武父子，采掇遺亡，至晉總括群書，裁二萬七千九百四十五卷。

translations.literal: When the father and son of Wei Wu gathered what had been lost, down to Jin's comprehensive compilation of all books, there were only twenty-seven thousand nine hundred forty-five scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao and his son gathered what had been lost, down to Jin's comprehensive compilation of all books, there were only 27,945 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 及永嘉之亂，洛都覆沒，靡有孑遺。

translations.literal: When the Yongjia turmoil came, the capital at Luoyang was overrun, and scarcely a survivor remained.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongjia turmoil came, the capital at Luoyang was overrun, and scarcely a survivor remained.

sentences.zh: 江表所存官書，凡三千一十四卷。

translations.literal: Official books preserved south of the Yangtze numbered three thousand fourteen scrolls in all.
translations.idiomatic: Official books preserved south of the Yangtze numbered 3,014 scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 至宋謝靈運造《四部書目錄》，凡四千五百八十二卷。

translations.literal: By the time Xie Lingyun of Song compiled the Bibliographic Catalogue in Four Sections, there were four thousand five hundred eighty-two scrolls in all.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Xie Lingyun of Song compiled the Bibliographic Catalogue in Four Sections, there were 4,582 scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 其後王儉復造書目，凡五千七十四卷。

translations.literal: Afterward Wang Jian again compiled a book catalogue, totaling five thousand seventy-four scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Wang Jian again compiled a book catalogue, totaling 5,074 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 南齊王亮、謝朏《四部書目》，凡一萬八千一十卷。

translations.literal: The Bibliographic Catalogue in Four Sections by Wang Liang and Xie Tiao of Southern Qi totaled eighteen thousand ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The Bibliographic Catalogue in Four Sections by Wang Liang and Xie Tiao of Southern Qi totaled 18,010 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 齊末兵火延燒秘閣，書籍煨燼。

translations.literal: At the end of Qi, military fires spread to the Secret Library, and the books were reduced to embers.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Qi, military fires spread to the Secret Library, and the books were reduced to embers.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝克平侯景，收公私經籍歸於江陵，凡七萬餘卷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang defeated Hou Jing, he collected public and private classics and books at Jiangling, totaling more than seventy thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang defeated Hou Jing, he collected public and private classics and books at Jiangling, totaling more than 70,000 scrolls.

translations.literal: Buddhist and Daoist books were reckoned among them.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist and Daoist books were reckoned among them.

translations.literal: When the Zhou armies entered Ying, all were burned to ashes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Zhou armies entered Ying, all were burned to ashes.

sentences.zh: 周武保定之中，官書裁盈萬卷。

translations.literal: During the Baoding era of Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou, the official books barely exceeded ten thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou in the Baoding period, the imperial collection scarcely amounted to ten thousand scrolls.

translations.literal: What was obtained in the pacification of Qi numbered only five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The books taken when Qi was conquered came to only five thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 及隋氏平陳，南北一統，秘書監牛弘奏請搜訪遺逸，著定書目，凡三萬餘卷。

translations.literal: When the Sui house pacified Chen and north and south were unified, the Director of the Secretariat Niu Hong memorialized requesting a search for lost and scattered works and the compilation of a fixed book catalog, totaling more than thirty thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: After the Sui conquered Chen and reunified the realm, Secretariat Director Niu Hong petitioned to recover lost texts and compile an official catalog, which came to more than thirty thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 煬帝寫五十副本，分為三品。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang had fifty duplicate copies made and divided them into three grades.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang ordered fifty duplicate sets made and ranked them in three grades.

sentences.zh: 國家平王世充，收其圖籍，溯河西上，多有沉沒，存者重復八萬卷。

translations.literal: When the state pacified Wang Shichong, it collected his maps and books; going up the Yellow River westward, many were sunk and lost, but what survived again amounted to eighty thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty defeated Wang Shichong, it seized his library; much was lost in transport up the western Yellow River, yet what remained still came to eighty thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 自武德已後，文士既有修纂，篇卷滋多。

translations.literal: From the Wude reign onward, since literati had undertaken compilation and editing, chapters and scrolls steadily increased.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wude era on, as scholars continued to compile and edit texts, the number of works kept growing.

sentences.zh: 開元時，甲乙丙丁四部書各為一庫，置知書官八人分掌之。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan period, the books of the four divisions Jia, Yi, Bing, and Ding each formed one repository, and eight officials knowing books were appointed to administer them separately.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign, the four library divisions each had its own vault, with eight bibliographic officers assigned to oversee them.

sentences.zh: 凡四部庫書，兩京各一本，共一十二萬五千九百六十卷。

translations.literal: All the books in the four repositories, one set in each of the two capitals, totaled one hundred twenty-five thousand nine hundred sixty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The four repositories held complete sets in both capitals, for a combined total of 125,960 scrolls.

translations.literal: All were written on hemp paper from Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: All were copied on hemp paper from Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 其集賢院御書，經庫皆鈿白牙軸，黃縹帶，紅牙籤，史書庫鈿青牙軸，縹帶，綠牙籤，子庫皆雕紫檀軸，紫帶，碧牙籤，集庫皆綠牙軸，硃帶，白牙籤，以分別之。

translations.literal: The imperial books of the Academy of Assembled Worthies: the Classics repository all had inlaid white ivory rollers, yellow silk ribbons, and red ivory markers; the Histories repository had inlaid green ivory rollers, light silk ribbons, and green ivory markers; the Masters repository all had carved rosewood rollers, purple ribbons, and jade-green ivory markers; the Collections repository all had green ivory rollers, vermilion ribbons, and white ivory markers, by which to distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Academy of Assembled Worthies, the Classics used white inlaid ivory rollers with yellow silk ties and red tags; Histories used green inlaid ivory rollers with pale silk ties and green tags; Masters used carved rosewood rollers with purple ties and blue-green tags; and Collections used green ivory rollers with vermilion ties and white tags, so each division could be told apart at a glance.
